pr_body:
Closes #61145.

This PR adds a quota-aware filesystem plugin to Elasticsearch. This plugin offers a way to provide user quota limits (specifically, total quota size and available quota size) to Elasticsearch, in an implementation-agnostic manner.

As part of this work, this PR also introduces the concept of "bootstrap only" plugins, which are excluded from the normal plugin loading process.

Finally, note that this implementation supports `createLink(...)`, since ES / Lucene use hard links where possible.

issue_context.title: Support for quota-aware file systems
issue_context.body:
Some users run Elasticsearch on file systems that enforce per-user quotas. The details of how such quotas work and how to query them are specific to each filesystem implementation, and there is no provision within the JVM to read them. This is unfortunate, as it means that when Elasticsearch calculates e.g. the percentage of available disk space when applying watermarks, it does so based on the entire disk's free space, not the free space that is actually available to Elasticsearch.

Java allows the default file system implementation to be overridden using the property `java.nio.file.spi.DefaultFileSystemProvider`. Elasticsearch could install a custom implementation that can account for filesystem quotas. Since the details of quota provision are completely outside the scope of Elasticsearch, this custom implementation would only provide an interface to communicate the quota and current disk usage. It would not contain logic for actually fetching this information.

We intend to make these changes for 6.8.x, 7.x (some future 7.x minor release), and master (8.0).

review_comments: Can we error if java opts is set for non bootstrap plugins?
I actually had that in, then removed it because of the validation I added to `bin/elasticsearch`, but I've put it back in to be on the safe side.

Just a note for future thinking there. We moved away from building all plugins and making them available to packaging tests, under the assumption plugins don't have platform specific behavior. Quota aware fs is a special case, I guess, but if we have any more cases like this, we should rethink how we model packaging tests for these plugins so as not to need special sysprops/setup for every one.
I can't do that until the changes are backported - I learnt that the hard way on another branch.

This can be done. There are 2 ways to handle the backports. One is to put CURRENT in master, change it on the backport, then go back to master and change all the occurrences. The other is to put the intended version in master and disable bwc tests (there is a global flag in the root build.gradle), backport, then re-enable bwc tests in master after the backport is complete. The latter has the advantages that the backport can be tested locally before committing to master, as well as only a single place to change (the bwc flag) on followup, instead of potentially multiple versioned conditional statements.
I believe this is the only place that I reference a version. I'll go for the former route I think.
